Messages.Author: hamdamcwa
Messages.Body:
I have been worrying about this for a while, but I think it's time to
come clean...

*ahem*

Hello, my name's Dave and my girlfriend is now a better VTES played
than me.

There you go.

Dammit.

She started playing about 6 weeks ago properly. Now, though, she has
built 3 pretty unassuming decks and is practically anassailable. Last
night she swept a 5 player table with a Lasombra toolbox deck (based
on the precon, but with a few extra bits thrown in - actually,
precious little thrown in, but enough to make it up to 90 cards).

2 weeks ago, she got 4 points with a deck based around the Tremere
precon. Actually, it is one of the scariest decks I have ever seen.

A week or so before that, she swept with a deck she borrowed from me,
decided it was rubbish, changed loads of it, and made a kick ass
mono-celerity deck (with guns).

Really, how do you stop it? I have no idea what has changed
(admittedly I haven't been putting the hours in in practicing play,
but even so, was I THAT BAD before that?), and I sure didn't teach her
how to play like that (she must have picked it all up from watching
from afar).

Ironically, I'm having the WORST run of play I've ever had. I have
played, like, 10 games in the last couple of weeks and always been out
first in all of them. But the fact that from almost nowhere my
girlfriend (who used to get all miffy with me and sulk that I was
going out to play cards and not pay attention to her etc etc) has
proven to be quite good is annoying in the extreme.

Has this happened to anyone else?

DH

Messages.Author: Sander
Messages.Body:


Not with VtES, but it did happen with one of my girlfriends for about
the same reason (I played Magic once a week). So yeah, some people are
just naturally talented. Or they are new and see new tricks that some
people who are playing longer can't see. I know it sometimes helps to
have a friend look over a deck you have build and just allow him
changes. Accept some of those suggestions, even if they sound strange to
you. It works.

--
Sander Hanevelt
